name: spec-driven-workflow
description: Use when a user request must become a spec, a plan, a todo list and a checklist that other agents can follow, or when checking whether the work on a spec is complete.
title: Spec, plan, todo, checklist
goal: Turn a request into four linked documents so an implementing agent can work without guessing and completion can be checked mechanically.
steps: Create the folder `docs/specs/<feature-name>/` (or the place the project already uses) and copy the four templates from `{{skill_dir}}/references/` into it: spec.md, plan.md, todo.md, checklist.md.

Spec: quote the request, then write numbered, testable requirements (functional and non-functional), scope, constraints, assumptions and open questions. Ask the user to answer open questions that block the plan; do not guess.

Plan: read the code first. Record the current state with file paths and line numbers you read. Decide where each change goes, whether to create a new file (only when no module owns the responsibility or a file would grow past about 400 lines or mix two responsibilities), the tests to write, risks and rollback. Map every requirement to work.

Todo: write ordered tasks with dependencies. For each: the exact file, what to change (function names, inputs, outputs, errors), what not to touch, how to comment (explain why, at most one short comment per non-obvious decision, a docstring on each new public function, no commented-out code), the test to write first, and the condition that means done.
Checklist: one line per requirement, per task and per quality gate. Every box starts unticked.

When work is reported done, run `python3 {{skill_dir}}/scripts/checklist_status.py checklist.md --require-evidence`. Exit 0 means complete. Exit 3 means it is not: list the open items and send the work back. Never tick a box without evidence and never delete an item to pass.
You write documents only. Do not edit source code.
output: Four files in the spec folder, a short summary of open questions, and (when asked) the checklist status.
gotchas: Every requirement needs a way to verify it.
A plan that has not read the code is a guess.
If the checklist has no checkbox lines the script reports not complete.
